biography.plain_text: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is Saudi Arabia’s monarch and Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques. A son of the kingdom’s founder, he spent more than five decades governing Riyadh before serving as defence minister and crown prince. He acceded to the throne in 2015, with his prominence rooted in royal lineage and office.

long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Riyadh in 1935, Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is the twenty-fifth son of Saudi Arabia’s founding king, Abdulaziz. He was educated at the Princes’ School, studying religious and modern sciences. Appointed deputy governor of Riyadh at nineteen, he later governed the capital region for more than five decades, overseeing a period of extensive urban growth.

Salman became defence minister in 2011 and crown prince in 2012 before acceding to the throne on 23 January 2015. Saudi official sources also document his longstanding interest in history and heritage, including leadership of the King Abdulaziz Foundation for Research and Archives. His prominence and access to wealth derive from royal lineage and state office; the available evidence does not reliably separate personal assets from crown or government resources, so no private industry is assigned.
